title: Discrete dynamics, coding and probability
description: A subject-first synthesis of discrete dynamics, symbolic coding, probability transport, harmonic analysis and Diophantine approximation. Complete proofs reach Tao's logarithmic orbit-minimum theorem, then combine conditioned mixing, integer fibres, sharp kernels and timed scale iteration into natural-density bounds. First-entrance costs retain a common endpoint across three clocks. Exact inverse branches, moving integer thresholds and weighted phase averages explain how to compare finite measures. Collatz is the running case study; every lesson has worked examples and four solved exercises.

level: Opening two lessons: proof-based undergraduate; later probability and number-theory lessons: graduate
prerequisites: Positive-integer arithmetic, induction and well-ordering; the second lesson also uses division with remainder. The third and fourth add elementary limits, real completeness, logarithms and integration of elementary functions. The fifth uses complex conjugation, complex exponentials and finite geometric sums. The sixth adds elementary differentiation and binomial coefficients; the seventh adds Euclidean vectors and repeated one-variable integration over boxes. Specialised return-map, coding, transport, Fourier, concentration, conditioning and local-probability arguments used here are proved in the lessons.

continuation_route.title: From finite Fourier analysis to weighted orbit minima
continuation_route.conclusion: Complete Fourier, renewal and fine-scale mixing proofs yield first-passage stabilization, compatible entrance limits, joint entrance laws without a threshold-count loss, and Tao's fixed-threshold and arbitrary-diverging-threshold conclusions. General weighted tightness is proved separately.

natural_density_continuation.available_results: Retained-statistic cancellation, joint Fourier and spatial mixing, exact conditioned clocks, paired likelihood and product estimates, exact integer fibres and first-passage intervals, residue discrepancy and an explicit finite boundary bound. A uniform binomial kernel bound and finite weighted transfer give the actual arithmetic fibre formula for each fixed coarse exponent theta in (0,1), with summed absolute error O((log x)^(-(1-theta)/2) sqrt(log log x)).
natural_density_continuation.rotation_results: Complete rational-grid discrepancy, Koksma and Abel proofs; mass-height averaging for unimodal profiles removes the truncation logarithm. Exact asymmetric-envelope mass, sampled mass and tails yield the sharp binomial kernel constant and error O(L^(-1/(2nu))+L^(-1/2)(log L)^3) for every slope satisfying the stated rational-separation bound. The square-root-of-two example has every premise proved.
natural_density_continuation.further_mathematics: Inselmann's full-horizon envelopes, their precise relation to the now completed same-orbit first-target synthesis, remaining companion refinements and survey-routed literature. Strengthen existing lessons where results are subsumed; no conjecture-solution requirement.
natural_density_continuation.endpoint_weight_results: Exact valuation cylinders and first-passage intervals give a reciprocal coefficient at most 1/2+(1/2)log(8/3)+3B^(-4997/600000). The terminal-weighted Chernoff calculation yields an exterior majorant with leading factor 1+log(8/3) and exponent64C^2/(log2)^3. Arbitrary endpoint filters and residue probabilities are retained. Mass-weighted assembly is proved; no automatic final density-exponent improvement follows from the coefficient refinement.
natural_density_continuation.lattice_profile_results: Strict-level multiplicities have prefix discrepancy at most one. Finite Gaussian summation and a fully explicit common-center local bound give the original mass1/Delta. Exact consecutive-time recurrences control zero-extension variation. Combining the common Gaussian with mass-height averaging removes the support-width logarithm from both intrinsic geometric profiles, giving power1/(2rho) when the tube tail is sufficiently small. All finite errors and exact clipping costs are retained; this is an analytic component, not by itself a new endpoint density exponent.
natural_density_continuation.strict_profile_results: Exact signed integer levels and strict successor threshold; neighboring negative-binomial profiles compared by an exact ratio and at most six boundary terms. Separate-mass and base-profile averaging bounds retain endpoint atoms, with full integral and summation-by-parts proofs. Sharp proportional-error absorption is charged to actual mass. These finite comparisons do not alone supply a genuine first-passage law or improve a final density exponent.
natural_density_continuation.finite_measure_comparison: Every positive odd endpoint satisfying its affine congruence decodes to a unique positive odd source with the prescribed valuations. Short-window terminal records are injective. Denominator replacement costs the relative error times actual mass; support replacement costs boundary mass with exact finite normalizing sums. The maximal offset is (3/2)^r-1, yielding the local exponent198939/200000 under the stated source length and endpoint bounds, without a new final density exponent.
natural_density_continuation.timed_results: Full timed target-set inclusion, summable geometric-scale iteration and disjoint interval cover. For odd inputs the clock log(N)/log(4/3)+CK*sqrt(log(N+2)*log(log(N+2)+2)) has fixed-target failure count O(X*(log H)^-tau), tau=5097587/77645938, uniformly for X,H>=2. Every diverging target is attained within that clock outside o(X) odd inputs. This is not an assertion for every orbit, a numerical asymptotic threshold or an optimal second-order term.
natural_density_continuation.entrance_results: Complete actual uniform-input entrance comparison, including a separate failure state and the mass of the common harmonic-residue profile. Summed error O(L^-tau + L^(-(1-theta)/2) sqrt(log L)), tau=5097587/77645938, for each fixed theta in (0,1). The choice theta=2/5 gives O(L^-tau). The proof controls multiplicities and excludes earlier crossings; the following timed lesson supplies the natural-density iteration.
natural_density_continuation.logarithmic_results: Complete reconstruction of Rhin's six-factor approximation: weighted divisibility, full-rank integral rows, exact rational extrema certificate and uniform transference. The lower bound for ||q log_2 3|| with exponent rho=38822969/5097587 supplies the actual logarithmic-slope kernel, whose error is O(L^(-1/(2rho))). The constant is positive but no numerical PNT threshold is computed.
natural_density_continuation.clock_transfer: A successful first-entrance path has distinct preceding states, so its additive logarithmic clock correction is O(log(k+1)). The exact telescope gives shortcut and ordinary leading coefficients2/log(4/3) and3/log(4/3), with the same square-root logarithmic allowance. Exact disjoint valuation fibres transport the fixed-target count with factor2, preserving one common endpoint and exponent tau. The general base-b count and zero-density equivalence are proved separately. No height, optimality or priority assertion.
natural_density_continuation.physical_profile_results: Exact logarithmic band partition and invertible time translation retain both strict level supports in the original padded time window. Rational logarithm bounds prove all scale, positivity and signed-level guards. Exact odd-integer denominators and exterior envelopes combine the analytic profile with arbitrary retained first-passage endpoint sets and residue probabilities, giving full reference-profile error O(N^-eta), eta=5097587/77645938, with the original endpoint mass. This does not by itself identify the genuine path event.
natural_density_continuation.prefix_passage_results: A bounded exponential stopping argument gives the exact two-sided geometric maximal rate, without a factor for the horizon. Exact residue transport with one ideal overflow state yields a full-prefix exceptional bound (2+o(1))N^(-C^2/4) for both actual band laws. Finite descent, time localization and shifted-endpoint bounds prove the word/endpoint correspondence in both directions on the good event, giving one symmetric-difference error uniformly in the target. This is not yet the remaining terminal mixing and probability assembly.
natural_density_continuation.weighted_assembly_results: Exact conditioned-cell identities and fibre averages retain every endpoint. A paired relative likelihood comparison and uniform fine mixing combine against actual total mass, not the number of cells. Exact shells, strict/half-open denominator comparison and the complete reference estimate give a common genuine first-passage law for both harmonic and uniform sampling on both branches, with error O((log B)^-eta), eta=5097587/77645938. Exact whole-block mixtures retain the upper endpoint. Completed probability laws include nonpassage without conditioning; their TV distance has the same rate, and the original reference mass is 1+O((log B)^-eta). No all-orbit, optimality, novelty or new formal certification claim.
natural_density_continuation.scheduled_transport_results: Exact information loss on merged states and weighted-overlap distance transport the genuine law to real thresholds without changing the source. A pointwise time inequality yields a finite recurrence with a separate scheduled-failure event. All four source-law comparisons permit uniform sampling throughout; the geometric sum gives odd-return coefficient100/(alpha log2) and ordinary coefficient(300/alpha+1)/log2 at exceptional exponent5097587/77645938. A disjoint interval count treats every input. These scheduled clocks are weaker than the existing drift clocks1/log(4/3) and3/log(4/3), which retain additional trajectory information.
natural_density_continuation.reverse_transport_results: Complete reverse-product and affine-defect coordinate maps; distinct exact and additive defects with exact concatenation. Odd-count rigidity gives the shell-clipped integer bound 1+floor(epsilon(2^(M+1)-1)); finite arbitrary-time-support transport survives all source restrictions. Distinct decreasing threshold ranks give additive loss <2(q+2)/(3r), and combined rank coefficient4(q+2)/(3r), with unchanged time support and landing set. Exact shortcut, odd-return and ordinary first-passage maps and inverses retain the original path. No final density-exponent or all-orbit conclusion follows from this finite improvement alone. A finite logarithmic path bound and final product loss now control every prefix odd count, every ordinary state, and actual first passages at every intermediate real level, with explicit constants.
natural_density_continuation.parity_envelope_results: Exact parity sampling, finite cosh potential, invertible reflection with both endpoint layers, explicit binomial prefactor, and exact affine comparison. The allowance beta=log_2(7/6)<1/4 gives all-rank quadratic prefactor2, fixed-entropy constant2exp(beta J_eta), and reduced startup m_eta=ceil(max(1,beta/eta)). The uniform shrinking-tolerance prefactor retains exp(beta J_tau) and eta M>=2beta. Full proofs and four solved exercises are in the existing lesson.
natural_density_continuation.stopped_chain_results: Exact endpoint exchange for literal controlled-prefix sets, finite first-failure transport without resampling, retained rank clock and same-path height. Complete final-shell summation yields stretched target exp((log n)^sigma) with exception O(X(log X)^(1+sigma/2) exp(-D(log X)^sigma)), and power target n^alpha with O(X^(1-alpha D)(log X)^(3/2)), D=I(eta/log_2 3)/log2 at the stated fixed parameters. All proofs and four solved exercises are internal; no all-orbit or optimality claim.
natural_density_continuation.iterated_pullback_results: Time-summed arbitrary-target transport has coefficient5/12 under the stated dyadic stage hypotheses. A full recurrence retains the closed exceptional exponent Dr^R and logarithmic power2R-1/2, with an explicit depth-dependent constant. An absorbing identity branch gives endpoint max(K,n^(r^R)); shortened horizons bound the original stopping times. Explicit parameters yield target n^alpha, ordinary height n^(1+beta), and shortcut/odd-return/ordinary leading coefficients2,1,3 times (1-alpha)/log(4/3), each with arbitrary positive tolerance and one exceptional count. Four solved exercises and bounded exact checks accompany the general written proofs.
natural_density_continuation.finite_survival_results: Finite stopped moments give an explicit two-boundary bound for arbitrary bounded centered increments, and auxiliary-height optimization yields min(1,2(h+L)/sqrt(vn)). An explicit Fourier binomial atom estimate combines with two independent outer survival constraints and a conditional middle estimate to prove C_B m^(-3/2)2^(-kappa*m) with a displayed constant. Two exact word-weight changes distinguish the centered law from the multiplicative-size-biased law, giving reciprocal maximum upper and lower bounds. Four solved exercises and exact bounded checks accompany full written proofs; no independent Collatz landing law or new endpoint-density theorem is inferred.
natural_density_continuation.timeout_coding_results: Exact affine extrema, literal timeout containment, an explicit cumulative time interval and original-source low-timeout estimate. The complete critical shell theorem combines these with one deterministic high-rank sequence and exact endpoint exchange, giving high charge O(M^(3/2-alpha)) without a boundary term. One endpoint has both centered clocks and both relative-height bounds, with maximum charge7/(3R). Independent arbitrary divergent target/height allowances give natural density one. For A>1/(2kappa), q=kappa*A-1/2, the joint target/time/height exceptional count is Theta(X/(log X)^q); the lower bound concerns height, not descent alone. The same retained path now satisfies uniform shortcut/parity/ordinary trajectory bounds and simultaneous actual first-passage profiles without another exception. Moving exponents with diverging critical margin and explicit iterated-logarithmic factors retain their rates. Fixed relative ceilings for sublinear targets exclude lower density at least2/(3C).
natural_density_continuation.same_orbit_synthesis: Theorem13 in the existing endpoint lesson intersects the fixed-target success event with the critical path on original positive inputs. Exact truncation/continuation and subtraction of a lower prefix clock from an upper total clock retain the existing square-root three-clock bounds, uniform paths, intermediate first passages and relative height nR. Failure count <=C0 X(log B)^(-gamma)+Ce X(log(X+2))^(-e)+14X/(3R), gamma=5097587/77645938, uniformly in B>=2,R>=4. Independent arbitrary divergent target/height functions follow. The lower joint bounds at polylogarithmic targets are not lower bounds for descent alone.
